posts.title: Decide slowly, act fast: why we picked 160ms for our agents
posts.description: Pick any place where machines meet people and you will find a number between 100 and 200 ms. In 2009 Jake Brutlag at Google added artificial delays to search results : 50 ms made no measurable difference, 100 ms already cost 0.2% of searches per user, 400 ms cost 0.6%, and the damage lingered for weeks after the delay was removed. posts.title: Talking while thinking
posts.description: Think of the last time you had a real conversation while driving. You merged, checked a mirror, glanced at the navigation, maybe decided to skip the next exit, and the conversation never stalled. Nobody calls this multitasking. It’s just what people do. posts.title: AI for humans
posts.description: Tomorrow I am giving one of the invited talks in the Applied Data Science track at KDD 2026 in Jeju, Korea. It’s a builder’s tour of some of the audio stack at Boson AI in three parts: how we train models that can hold a conversation, how we design benchmarks that tell us whether the next model is actually better, and how we decide which benchmarks are worth running at all.
